organizeYourProjectsWorkWithCodexAgentsA: Organize your projects, work with Codex agents and keep track of shared knowledge, actions and deliverables. This guide explains where to start and how the features fit together.
platformGuideIntroduction: The platform brings people, conversations, files, knowledge, tasks, deliverables and automations together within each project. This guide presents the available workflows and the important rules to understand.
guideGettingStartedCreate: Create a project from the + beside Projects and give it a clear name.
guideGettingStartedOrganize: Add participants, optionally select a project manager and prepare people groups.
guideGettingStartedConfigure: Add shared knowledge, attach the useful workspaces and select the project's apps and MCP servers.
guideGettingStartedWork: Create a conversation or the manager you need: tasks, deliverables or automations.
guideGettingStartedReview: Follow approval requests, review the results and keep durable decisions in project knowledge.
guideProjectsOverview: A project is the shared scope for participants, conversations, workspaces, knowledge, tasks, deliverables, automations and connectors. Home brings together projects, upcoming deadlines and actions that need attention.
guideProjectsResources: Use a project's + menu to create a Codex conversation, a simple conversation or a resource. A project can contain several task managers, but only one deliverables manager and one automation manager.
guidePeopleAndAccessScope: An administrator can view every project. An active standard user only sees projects they participate in; conversations, files, knowledge, tasks and deliverables follow the same scope. Codex execution, terminals and server automations remain restricted to administrators.
guidePeopleAndAccessOrganization: Administrators manage participants, the project manager and people groups. The project manager and groups organize work: they grant no additional access and do not restrict participant access.
guideConversationsTypes: A simple conversation answers through the OpenAI API without running tools. A Codex conversation can work in a workspace, inspect or modify files and run commands according to its permissions. Give it a goal, an expected result and verifiable constraints.
guideConversationsControls: The conversation displays its activity, quota usage and approval or user-input requests. Available / commands can set a goal, enter Plan mode, start a review, compact context or send feedback.
guideConversationsBranches: Editing an earlier message creates a branch instead of silently rewriting history. The version switcher and branch graph let you compare paths; deleting a branch may include descendants and therefore shows a preview before confirmation.
guideWorkspacesStructure: The Locations and connections tab separates the local space managed by Mergeron, other local folders, and external Git, SSH/SFTP or FTP/FTPS connections. The primary space remains permanent and identified by the project ID. Each conversation keeps its own active working directory. Internal .mergeron data is hidden by default in the project file listing; administrators can show a technical view without changing existing permissions.
guideWorkspacesViews: Within a conversation, tabs let you move between the discussion, files, editors and terminals without losing their current state. User files remain separate from the reserved .mergeron system directory used for application history and metadata.
guideKnowledgeDocuments: Project knowledge contains shared instructions, durable facts and decisions. It is stored in the primary workspace and added to the context of new project exchanges; it never replaces security rules.
guideKnowledgeProposals: A conversation can propose information to remember, but it is not added automatically. An administrator reviews proposals, accepts useful changes or edits the shared documents directly.
guideTasksStructure: A main task has a priority, dates, an assignee, an estimate, labels and validation criteria. It can contain manual subtasks or subtasks assigned to an agent. Dependencies connect main tasks and cycles are rejected.
guideTasksViews: Each manager offers four views: Advice to analyze work, Board to organize cards, Planning for dates and dependencies, and Journal to review changes. Several task managers can coexist in one project.
guideTasksAgents: AI assistance can propose a plan, split a task or suggest replanning before anything is applied. Only subtasks can be executed by a Codex agent. A person must review and validate the result before completion.
guideDeliverablesStructure: A deliverable describes an expected result, criteria and status. Its main task drives the owner, due date and progress. Related work is available from Main task.
guideDeliverablesDocuments: Each document has its own version history. It can be previewed, downloaded, replaced, soft-deleted and restored. Office files open in OnlyOffice when it is configured.
guideDeliverablesLifecycle: Overview, Documents, Validation, History, Main task and Access separate the uses. The lifecycle goes from Draft to In constitution, then Finalized and Archived. Required validation applies to the snapshot frozen at finalization.
guideAutomationsManager: A project can have one automation manager containing several automated tasks. Once it exists, the Automations entry in the + menu opens that resource directly.
guideAutomationsRuns: Each automation defines its purpose, target and manual or scheduled trigger. Review its status, history and results. Creating, changing and running automations is restricted to administrators.
guideIntegrationsSelection: Project settings let you enable available Codex apps and MCP servers independently. The selection applies to new project conversations; an already loaded conversation keeps the configuration it started with.
guideIntegrationsAuthentication: OAuth connections and plugins are configured in administration. Credentials remain in persistent server storage and are not copied into the project. A connector must be globally available before it can be enabled for a project.
guideDocumentsPreview: The file explorer opens text files and images, displays PDFs in the built-in viewer and uses OnlyOffice for supported formats. Archives can be browsed within the platform's protections and limits.
guideDocumentsSafety: File access depends on the project that owns its workspace. A symbolic link, document URL or conversation association grants no additional access. If project access is removed, close and reopen the affected editors.
guideAdministrationAccount: Codex → Account shows your identity and quotas. Other Codex tabs are disabled without a connected account. This connection is separate from your platform session.
guideAdministrationSettings: Administrators manage people, authentication, Codex models, simple chat, terminals, files, security, the database and integrations. Codex CLI settings support first installation, updates and returning to the previous version.
guideAdministrationOperations: Operations tools provide the global file browser, terminal, logs and diagnostics. They apply to the whole server and require more care than project-scoped views.
guideGoodPracticesReview: Treat agent answers and changes as work to review. Inspect file changes, answer approval requests explicitly and have a person validate tasks and deliverables before declaring them complete.
guideGoodPracticesPersistence: Conversations, the database, configuration and tokens are persistent, but persistence is not a backup. Back up Codex state and workspaces together before an important update, migration or trial that may change data.
guideProjectAdministrationOverview: Project tabs bring together general information, people, the journal, settings, workspaces, knowledge and connectors. Participants can view the items they are allowed to access; structural and configuration changes are restricted to administrators.

useASimpleConversationToAskQuestionsAndD: Use a simple conversation to ask questions and discuss ideas. A work agent can inspect and modify files and run commands with the tools and permissions available to it. Describe your goal, the expected result and any constraints.
eachConversationHasItsOwnHistorySharedPr: Each conversation has its own history. Shared project knowledge supplies common context to subsequent messages. Follow the conversation status and respond when the agent requests a decision or approval.
everyProjectHasAPermanentPrimaryWorkspac: Every project has a permanent primary workspace identified by the project ID. Renaming the project keeps this directory. The primary workspace can only be removed when the project itself is deleted.
secondaryWorkspacesAttachOtherWorkingDir: Secondary workspaces attach other working directories to the project. The active workspace is the directory used by a conversation; it can be primary or secondary. User files and the reserved .mergeron system directory have separate purposes.
useTheProjectKnowledgeTabToManageCommonI: Use the project knowledge tab to manage common instructions, useful facts and decisions. These documents live in the primary workspace and provide shared context to conversations in the project.
importantInformationDiscussedInAConversa: Important information discussed in a conversation is not automatically established as project knowledge. Review memory proposals and accept useful changes, or edit the shared documents directly when your role permits it.
addATaskManagerWhenTheProjectNeedsAction: Add a task manager when the project needs action tracking. Create tasks and subtasks, assign participants, set deadlines and estimates, and follow progress through the board and planning views.
agentAssistanceHelpsCarryOutWorkLinkedTo: Agent assistance helps carry out work linked to a task. Review the result and its validation criteria before marking the action complete. A project can contain several task managers.
aProjectCanAddOneAutomationManagerContai: A project can add one automation manager containing several automations. Once it exists, choosing Automations again in the + menu opens that manager.
configureWhatEachAutomationShouldDoItsTa: Configure what each automation should do, its target and its manual or scheduled execution. Check its run history and results. Server execution and automation management require administrator access.
addTheOptionalDeliverablesManagerWhenThe: Add the optional deliverables manager when the project needs identifiable outputs. Each record describes the expected result, responsible person, deadline and validation criteria, and can link tasks and conversations. There is one manager per project.
workingFilesLiveInThePrimaryWorkspaceSub: Working files live in the primary workspace. Submitting a version creates a separate copy for review. Explicit validation sets the reference version; preparing the next version preserves it. Removing a record or manager preserves the physical files.
availableActionsDependOnYourRoleAdminist: Available actions depend on your role. Administrators manage platform settings, integrations and server execution. Standard users use the features allowed by their account; project participation also lets you assign work to the right person.
projectSettingsEnableOrDisableAvailableA: Project settings enable or disable available apps and MCP servers for that project. Platform Codex settings configure the server defaults, model behaviour and CLI maintenance. Ask an administrator if a feature is unavailable.
